advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test: source=status with no last-pass/lock ref yields NEVER_RUN and falls back to the GitHub bootstrap witness (assert the bootstrap-suffixed status_msg).
evidence: scripts/canary_bridge.py: `if verdict == "NEVER_RUN": ... return _check_github_heartbeat(runner, environ, now_epoch, window_hours, bootstrap=True)`
scripts/canary_bridge.py: status_msg `+ (" (last-pass producer bootstrap fallback)." if bootstrap else "")`
ABSENCE: `search_files` for `bootstrap` under tests/scripts returns only unrelated autodeploy hits; no status-source test plants zero refs to trigger NEVER_RUN
advisory.finding: The status-source NEVER_RUN -> GitHub run-history bootstrap fallback path is untested. `_check_status_heartbeat` routes a NEVER_RUN verdict to `_check_github_heartbeat(..., bootstrap=True)`, which appends the distinct ' (last-pass producer bootstrap fallback).' suffix; no test drives a NEVER_RUN snapshot under source=status to assert the fallback runs and the bootstrap message is emitted.
scenarios: Producer-first rollout where old producers have written no last-pass ref yet — the canary must still report health via the GitHub bootstrap witness
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a SequenceRunner test returning `_status("NEVER_RUN")` for the bridge-status call plus a `('gh','api')` fresh-run payload, and assert stale=false with the '(last-pass producer bootstrap fallback)' suffix.

evidence: scripts/canary_bridge.py: `if source not in {"status", "github-api"}: print(f"::error::REBAR_CANARY_HEARTBEAT_SOURCE must be status or github-api, got {source!r}") return 1`

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test: a RUNNING snapshot without a positive lock_lease_secs exits 1 with the 'omitted a positive lock lease' error and does not sleep.
evidence: scripts/canary_bridge.py: `lease = status.get("lock_lease_secs") ... if not isinstance(lease, (int, float)) or isinstance(lease, bool) or lease <= 0: print("::error::RUNNING status omitted a positive lock lease") return 1`
ABSENCE: `search_files` for `omitted a positive lock lease` under tests returns (no matches); all RUNNING test snapshots include `lease_secs`
advisory.finding: The RUNNING-with-missing/invalid-lease guard is untested. `_check_status_heartbeat` returns 1 with '::error::RUNNING status omitted a positive lock lease' when a RUNNING snapshot has no positive numeric `lock_lease_secs`; the existing RUNNING tests always supply lease_secs, so this guard has no coverage.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add tests: RUNNING first snapshot then a second snapshot resolving to HEALTHY/PAUSED (stale=false, recovered message) and to a non-healthy verdict (stale=true).
evidence: scripts/canary_bridge.py: `second_verdict = str(second.get("verdict") or "INDETERMINATE"); recovered = second_verdict in {"HEALTHY", "PAUSED"}; _append_outputs(..., stale="false" if recovered else "true", ...)`

ABSENCE: test_canary_bridge_heldout.py RUNNING tests use two RUNNING snapshots (advance/stalled) only; test_canary_status_refs_heldout.py plants a lock on the 2nd call (still RUNNING). No test resolves the 2nd snapshot to HEALTHY/PAUSED or to FAILED.
advisory.finding: The RUNNING second-observation 'resolved-to-non-RUNNING' branch is untested. When the second snapshot's verdict is not RUNNING, `_check_status_heartbeat` classifies HEALTHY/PAUSED as recovered (stale=false) and any other verdict as stale=true; existing canary tests only cover second-observation RUNNING advance (advanced) and unchanged-lease (crashed), never a mid-witness transition to HEALTHY/PAUSED or to a failed verdict.
scenarios: A pass completes (HEALTHY) or is paused (PAUSED) between the two observations, or transitions to FAILED/FOREIGN

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Guard the canary's `git fetch '+refs/reconciler/*:refs/reconciler/*'` with `|| true` (matching reconcile-bridge.yml) so a transient/absent-ref fetch does not hard-fail the job before status classification.
evidence: reconcile-bridge-canary.yml:102-104: `set -euo pipefail` then `git fetch origin '+refs/reconciler/*:refs/reconciler/*'` (no `|| true`)

reconcile-bridge.yml:136: `git fetch origin '+refs/reconciler/*:refs/reconciler/*' || true` — producer guards the identical fetch as best-effort, comment: 'Best-effort: absent refs (first run / file backend) simply fetch nothing.'
canary_bridge.py:190-199: NEVER_RUN bootstrap fallback exists but is only reached if `rebar bridge status` runs; a failed ref fetch aborts the job before the check step.
advisory.finding: The canary's new reconciler-ref fetch runs under `set -euo pipefail` without the `|| true` guard the producer workflow uses for the identical fetch, so a transient fetch failure hard-fails the canary job at the mount step instead of falling through to the NEVER_RUN/github-api bootstrap path the design intends.
scenarios: Transient network/auth blip during the reconciler-ref fetch on an otherwise-healthy environment
First-run / producer-first rollout where reconciler refs are absent
advisory.suggested_fix: Append `|| true` to the fetch: `git fetch origin '+refs/reconciler/*:refs/reconciler/*' || true`, mirroring reconcile-bridge.yml:136.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the 480s lease-sleep ceiling against wall-clock already consumed by checkout/pip-install/setup and the post-check steps so the 480s sleep cannot push the job past its 10-minute timeout (e.g. lower the ceiling or compute remaining budget).
evidence: canary_bridge.py:205-211: rejects `lease > 480` citing 'the fixed 10-minute job timeout', then `time.sleep(lease)`
reconcile-bridge-canary.yml:74: `timeout-minutes: 10` (600s)
reconcile-bridge-canary.yml:115-119: `pip install .` step runs before the check step (line 166-172), consuming wall-clock from the same 600s budget
reconcile-bridge-canary.yml:180-231: heartbeat-alert, binding-drift, and flush steps run AFTER the check step and also share the 600s budget
advisory.finding: The canary can sleep up to 480s for the RUNNING lease re-observation, but that budget is measured against the 10-minute job timeout while checkout, `pip install .`, and other setup steps run BEFORE the check step; a slow install plus the 480s sleep plus the post-check alert-lifecycle/flush steps can approach or exceed the 600s job timeout.
scenarios: A reconciler pass holding a ~480s lease coincides with a cold pip cache / slow runner
RUNNING re-observation followed by an alert-lifecycle that must open/comment on a ticket and flush pushes

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm (or document) that RUNNING should ignore holder identity vs --target; if not, gate RUNNING on the live lock holder matching the resolved target so a foreign live holder is not reported healthy.
evidence: last_pass.py:179-186: 'if pause is not None: verdict = "PAUSED" / elif lock is not None: verdict = "RUNNING" / elif record is None: ... / elif record["environment_id"] != target: verdict = "FOREIGN"'
last_pass.py:26: 'HEALTHY_VERDICTS = frozenset({"HEALTHY", "PAUSED", "RUNNING"})'
The FOREIGN check is only reached when lock is None, so a foreign holder that currently holds the lease is reported RUNNING/healthy.
dropped.finding: In snapshot(), a live lock unconditionally yields verdict RUNNING (and RUNNING is in HEALTHY_VERDICTS) without comparing the lock holder's identity to the resolved target. A live pass from a FOREIGN producer therefore reports a healthy RUNNING status rather than surfacing the identity mismatch that a completed FOREIGN record would produce.
